note:
ISO 2026-W09 runs from February 23 through March 1. Saturn and Neptune are separated by about 0.2° in geocentric ecliptic longitude at the Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot.

**Naked eye:** 🌓 First Quarter — 12:27:37 UTC. Moderate moonlight makes timing and local sky position important for faint targets. Use Aludra, Gomeisa, Castor, Procyon, Pollux as the week’s fixed-sky framework.

**Planets:** Moon: Naked eye; magnitude -9.4; direct motion; 33.1% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Jupiter in ecliptic longitude Feb 27 07:10 UTC. Conjunction with Uranus in ecliptic longitude Feb 23 22:28 UTC. Mercury: In solar glare; magnitude 0.0; direct motion; 34.5% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Station Feb 26 06:48 UTC: turns retrograde. Conjunction with Venus in ecliptic longitude Feb 28 05:34 UTC. Venus: In solar glare; magnitude -3.9; direct motion; 98.1% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Mercury in ecliptic longitude Feb 28 05:34 UTC. Mars: In solar glare; magnitude 1.1; direct motion; 99.6% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Ceres: Telescope; magnitude 9.1; direct motion; 98.3% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Jupiter: Naked eye; magnitude -2.5; retrograde motion; 99.5% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Moon in ecliptic longitude Feb 27 07:10 UTC. Saturn: Naked eye; magnitude 1.0; direct motion; 99.9% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Uranus: Binoculars; magnitude 5.7; direct motion; 99.9% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Moon in ecliptic longitude Feb 23 22:28 UTC. Neptune: Telescope; magnitude 7.8; direct motion; 100.0% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Pluto: Substantial telescope; magnitude 14.6; direct motion; 100.0% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot.

**Binoculars:** Trace Monoceros’s charted figure in the finder, then identify α Mon at its charted position.

**Small telescope:** Concentrate on M47, M46, M93. Increase magnification only after the target and surrounding pattern are secure.

**Substantial telescope:** No fixed-sky Calendar object is classified as requiring a substantial telescope this week.

story_candidates.dek: Aludra is a stellar reference in CMa used by the weekly observing calendar.
story_candidates.body:
Why it is here: The Calendar selected Aludra for this week’s fixed-sky observing sequence; its permanent object identity ties the weekly entry to the same star used by the finder.

How to find it: Establish the preserved CMa constellation figure from its labeled reference stars, then use the target’s plotted position rather than searching for an isolated star.
